criteria.criterion: defaults.toml has a new entry (own id, statement, source naming records/interventions/2026-10/20261026-180231-tf2p.json) stating: at 3 rejected or failed attempts in one retry lineage, Athena stops retrying, records the repeated findings and queues one narrower re-scope or split request; and states whether it is enforced by mechanism.
criteria.evidence: I read the diff. The new `[[default]] id = "lineage-limit"` says: at 3 rejected or failed attempts in one lineage Athena makes no 4th attempt, records the findings that repeated, and queues one narrower re-scope or split request. It says "It is enforced by mechanism in the drain", and its source names the intervention record. The record in the evidence snapshot (a five-attempt lineage stopped and re-queued narrower) matches the source text. The test that parses the real defaults.toml passed, and so did the reader budget tests (system_facts_budgets_match_computed).

criteria.criterion: A lineage-length helper in crates/athena-core/src/reading/retry.rs (built on the existing retries_by_job/job_history chain) counts the rejected or failed attempts in a lineage, and the limit 3 is a named constant or config value, visible in the diff.
criteria.evidence: The retry.rs diff adds `pub const LINEAGE_ATTEMPT_LIMIT: usize = 3`, `lineage_attempts`, `lineage_chain` and `lineage_stops`. They are built on `job_history` and a new `retries_in`, which was split out of `retries_by_job` and keeps the same behavior. Rejected, failed and timed-out jobs count. 15 core lineage unit tests pass. They cover the constant, landed, dropped, stale and foreign jobs, cycles, and that retries_by_job gives the same result as before.

criteria.criterion: A new test in crates/athena-cli/tests/drain.rs (or retry.rs) builds a lineage with 3 rejected attempts and shows the drain starts no 4th attempt; run `cargo test` and the named test passes.
criteria.evidence: In `a_lineage_with_three_rejected_attempts_gets_no_fourth_attempt`, two attempts are rejected by hand, then the drain runs a queued retry q with max_jobs 2, so it has room for a 4th. The test asserts that j1, j2 and q are Rejected, that lineage_attempts is [j1,j2,q], that no 'try again on q' exists, that the passed-over line names the lineage stop, and that no 'failed twice' or job-limit line appears. A second test, `a_queued_retry_of_a_lineage_with_three_failures_is_not_read_or_run`, shows a queued 4th attempt gets zero agent invocations and is closed as Dropped. Both pass.

criteria.criterion: The same or a sibling test shows exactly one narrower re-scope/split request is queued in place of the retry, and that its text carries the findings that repeated across the attempts; run `cargo test`.
criteria.evidence: `the_lineage_stop_queues_one_narrower_request_that_carries_the_repeated_findings` checks that exactly one request carries the `Lineage <j1>:` marker, that its title starts 'Re-scope or split', and that it holds the repeated finding 'the description lists no callers' and all three attempt ids. It has fewer acceptance bullets than the root, and none of them is a root bullet. Asking to queue again returns the same id and leaves head unchanged. The tests for the stop on the item's second attempt, the once-per-root unit test and the core matching tests also pass.

findings.summary: An unrelated default's reader text changes to keep the reader budget.
findings.evidence: The buy-first statement changes ';' to '. ', so `DefaultsModel::render` (first_sentence, defaults.rs:77) now shows the reader only 'Adopt good, maintained tools and crates before building.'. The reader loses 'build only for needs they don't meet, and record the call.' This keeps the reader budget at 1997 of 2000 (budgets tests pass). It is disclosed in CHANGELOG and was in the plan, but it is a small behavior change outside the request. Raising the budget instead would need docs/system-facts.md, which is not a deliverable.

findings.summary: Findings are matched as repeats by word overlap, a heuristic.
findings.evidence: Two located findings in the same file count as one when they share at least 2 content words that make up more than half of the shorter list. This can pair different findings. The effect is limited: matching only decides which items the narrower request lists. It never decides whether a lineage is stopped, which is an exact count of job states. Unit tests cover the contrasting pairs.

findings.summary: The reading said the change would reuse retry_findings' text. It adds new Observed/repeated_items code instead.
findings.evidence: No call to retry_findings appears in the diff. The new code collects unmet criteria and blocking findings itself.

summary: The change passes: all 8 criteria are met and nothing blocks it. It adds a `lineage-limit` default that cites the intervention record and says it is enforced by mechanism, plus a constant `LINEAGE_ATTEMPT_LIMIT = 3` and lineage-counting helpers in retry.rs built on `job_history` and `retries_by_job`. The drain checks the limit in two places: when it plans (a queued retry of a lineage already at 3 is never read, and is dropped) and after each failed attempt (the attempt that makes 3 is the last). It queues one narrower 'Re-scope or split' request per lineage, carrying the findings that repeated. I ran the planned targeted tests in this snapshot and all pass: the drain tests show no 4th attempt with room for one, zero agent calls for a queued 4th, exactly one narrower request holding the repeated finding, and no second request on a second ask; the core lineage tests, the once-per-root unit test, all of tests/retry.rs (the new hand-retry override test included) and the reader budget tests pass too. Athena's recorded fmt, clippy and test runs passed. The 8 changed files are exactly the 8 deliverables, and nothing under records/ changed. Two things are worth knowing: the buy-first default was reworded so the reader now sees only its first sentence (done to stay within the reader budget, and disclosed in the changelog), and findings are matched as repeats by word overlap, which affects only the text of the narrower request, not whether a lineage stops.
